candidates.original_title: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect
candidates.description: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect
candidates.citation_sentence: Proverbio and colleagues [2] argue that the McGurk effect is absent in highly trained musicians.
candidates.notes: The paper reports two analyses (replication and targeted) but these are two analyses of the same experiment, not separate entries. The replication found that musicians are subject to the McGurk effect, contradicting the original claim.

candidates.original_title: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect
candidates.description: Skilled musicians do not experience the McGurk effect when audiovisual speech stimuli conflict.
candidates.citation_sentence: As Proverbio and colleagues [2] had 30 musicians and 30 non-musicians in the critical conditions, we set a goal of 60 musicians and 60 non-musicians; as we ran the participants in groups, we scheduled slightly more participants than necessary in case of no-shows.
candidates.notes: The paper reports a close replication using modified procedures and two analysis schemes. Both analyses found a robust McGurk effect among musicians, contradicting the original study's conclusion that musicians were not subject to the effect.
